question: Pour comparer les coûts de logement d'un propriétaire et d'un locataire dans le recensement canadien, suffit-il de comparer le versement hypothécaire au loyer?
generated_answer: Le versement hypothécaire ne représente qu'une partie du coût de logement d'un propriétaire. You can compare the cost of housing for homeowners and renters by calculating the cost of housing as a percentage of household income. The Census of Population collects information on the total household income and the shelter expenses (which include mortgage payments, property taxes and condominium fees, rent, electricity, heating fuel, water and sewerage, contents insurance and the monthly condominium fee). The cost of housing is calculated as a percentage of total household income. The Census of Population also collects information on the tenure of the dwelling. Tenure refers to whether the household owns or rents its dwelling. The household is considered to own the dwelling if it is a dwelling owned by a member of the household, or by a business in which a member of the household has a proprietorship interest. The household is considered to rent the dwelling if it is a dwelling rented by a member of the household, or by a business in which a member of the household has a proprietorship interest. The Census of Population also collects information on the type of household. A household refers to a person or a group of persons who occupy the same dwelling and do not have a usual place of residence elsewhere in Canada. A household of one person may be composed of one person with no family members, or one person with family members (with family members being non-resident). A household of two or more persons refers to a group of persons who share the same dwelling and are related by blood, marriage, common-law or adoption. A household of two or more persons may be composed of a census family (with all members being related by blood, marriage, common-law or adoption) or a non-census family (with at least one member being related by blood, marriage, common-law or adoption). The Census of Population also collects information on the number of persons in the household. The number of persons in a household refers to the number of persons who occupy the same dwelling and do not have a usual place of residence elsewhere in Canada.
